subject: Recap + next steps — stakeholder map, SLA targets, procurement timeline
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@brightbridgehealth.com>, Mark Liu <mark.liu@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps — stakeholder map, SLA targets, procurement timeline

Hi Sarah / Mark —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve pasted the rough stakeholder map and asks below; Marcus and Lauren are looped in for technical and contracting follow-up.

Call highlights (10m):
- Primary use case: inference for clinical triage recommendations (API-based, real-time).
- Deployment preference: private VPC in AWS (data residency + audit controls).
- Rough scale: 200–500 qps peak for NLG prompts, burst to 800 during batch windows.

Stakeholder map (as understood):
- Economic buyer: Sarah Turner — Head of ML Platform (owns budget + vendor selection).
- Security / Compliance: Security team (procurement contact Mark Liu for contracts + procurement flow).
- Legal: In-house counsel (we expect a standard DPA + SOC 2 attestation).
- Platform owner / integrator: ML infra team (will work with Marcus on integration).

Decision criteria we heard (please confirm or correct):
1) Latency: p95 <= 350 ms for single-turn requests (target).
2) Reliability: 99.9% availability SLA for production endpoints.
3) Cost: target unit economics to fit budgeting — rough internal target is to keep inference spend growth linear with usage (we flagged batching/quantization savings).
4) Deployment: Private VPC preferred; on-prem considered only for air-gapped reg cases.
5) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II + KMS support for keys.

Attachments: I’m including the BrightBridge security questionnaire you mentioned (attached to this thread for our internal review) and a short SLA draft that covers our standard 99.9% + credits model.

Proposed next steps and owners: 
- Sarah: confirm the economic buyer and procurement timeline — is Q4 vendor selection target? (reply)
- Mark / Procurement: send any specific vendor docs or PO process steps we should align to (attach to reply).
- Marcus (SE): propose a short technical proof plan (2-week pilot, can run in your VPC).
- Lauren (Sales Manager): we’ll assemble a commercial term sheet after procurement asks are confirmed.

Tentative timeline: pilot kickoff week of 2026-09-27, legal/procurement review in parallel, decision by mid/late October if timelines hold.

Thanks — I’ll hold on scheduling until we hear back on timeline.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[evelyn_hart@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: BrightBridge_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx) — please fill or point to the canonical doc; SLA_draft_Redwood_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Liu <mark.liu@brightbridgehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — stakeholder map, SLA targets, procurement timeline

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear recap — this aligns with our internal notes. A few clarifications: 

1) Economic buyer — that is correct (I’ll own vendor selection but the CFO signs off on >$500k commits).
2) Latency — the 350 ms p95 target is acceptable as a goal; for safety-critical endpoints we may require p95 <= 250 ms and will scope that separately.
3) Procurement timeline — we’re aiming for vendor selection by 2026-10-18; procurement/legal will do standard review (we expect 2–3 weeks once we have the questionnaire + SOW).
4) Security docs — I’ve attached the completed top-level questionnaire (see short answers in the doc). We still need your SOC 2 report and a list of sub-processors.

Action items from our side: 
- Mark (procurement) will follow up with vendor onboarding steps and our PO template.
- I’ll introduce legal to your contracts team if we move to SOW/contracting.

One ask on cost: can you sketch a representative monthly cost model for 300 qps steady with the pilot profile you suggested (we can take a ballpark next-day)? Marcus, can you propose the pilot architecture (VPC peering or managed private) and expected token burn profile?

Appreciate it — speak soon.

— Sarah
Sarah Turner
Head of ML Platform | BrightBridge Health
sarah.turner@brightbridgehealth.com

Attachment: BrightBridge_Security_Questionnaire_filled.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — stakeholder map, SLA targets, procurement timeline

Evelyn / team —

Quick note from procurement: our typical vendor onboarding asks are below. Please send over the named items and a commercial contact we can reference on the PO: 
- W9 or tax form (US vendor)
- Standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) or draft SOW template
- SOC 2 Type II report and any relevant penetration test summaries
- Insurance certificate (cyber liability)
- Bank wiring details for net-30 payment terms (we can discuss faster terms if needed)

If you can provide the MSA + SOC2 + insurance by 2026-09-20, procurement can start intake and we’ll schedule a vendor risk review.

Mark
Mark Liu
Director of Procurement | BrightBridge Health
mark.liu@brightbridgehealth.com

Hi Sarah / Mark —

Thanks for the notes. Quick technical outline for the pilot (attached as a one-pager in the Drive link):
- Architecture: private VPC peering into Redwood-managed inference nodes (we can also do a fully customer-managed on-prem option)
- Latency expectations: with our optimized serving runtime we typically see p95 in the 180–300 ms range for the family of models you described at ~300 qps with batching; critical endpoints can be tuned to the 220–250 ms p95 band with memory/kv-cache pinning.
- Token profile: expect ~2.5k tokens per request average during the pilot (including context); that maps to ~180M tokens/day at 300 qps sustained — we’ll provide a cost sketch as requested.
- Pilot scope: 2-week sandbox + 2-week scale test; SE will deliver integration checklist and sample IaC snippets.

Next steps from our side:
- Marcus to share pilot runbook + cost sketch by 2026-09-16.
- Evelyn to follow up on MSA + SOC2 docs for procurement.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
